text:
Alex DeBrincat has no points in seven straight games, and Detroit has lost a lot of them. That's the hard version of his season. The softer version: he has 16 points in 22 games, he's shooting 9.1% against a league norm of 13.3%, and he has 7 goals on 8.8 expected (the quality of his chances).

The worry is that the drought isn't all bad luck. Our numbers note the chances have thinned during the pointless run (6.0 expected points, 3 actual over ten games). He's still driving play at five on five, with Detroit taking 57.4% of expected goals with him on the ice, so the possession is there and the finish isn't.

The Red Wings have bigger problems than one cold winger. Dylan Larkin has refused to play until he's traded, and DeBrincat dropped the gloves with Sam Bennett in a blown 4-1 lead against Florida, which had some fans calling for him to wear the C. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among 401 forwards last season. That player is still in there; watch whether his looks from the slot come back.
headline: DeBrincat has gone cold while Detroit sinks
